Definition: from an old noun ἐτεός (fitness); adjusted, i.e. ready:--prepared, (made) ready(-iness, to our hand).
BiblicalUsage: hétoimos — prepared, ready. That is the whole of it, and it is enough: 17 occurrences, and in Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John the meaning never wavers. I keep coming back to the simple reading because the simple reading is the true one.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe hétoimos matters because God prepares His people for the work He has prepared for them. I hold that the simple reading is the true one, and I will not trade it for a clever one.
RelatedEvents: The Wedding Feast; The Parable of the Watchful Servants
